positioning: Russia's rugged forest cat. A powerful triple-coated giant with a tender streak.
story: The Siberian is Russia's native cat and its national treasure, a hardy longhair that survived centuries of brutal winters in the forests and villages of Siberia. It is an ancient natural breed, not a designed one, and it shows in every line of its powerful body.

That body is built for cold. A dense, water-resistant triple coat, a full neck ruff, and a bushy tail let it shrug off snow, and big tufted paws carry it over it. Under the fur it is muscular and surprisingly heavy, an athletic jumper that lands like a cat half its size.
Siberians are slow to mature, taking up to five years to fill out. They are playful, fearless, and dog-like, often fetching toys, following their people, and taking a curious interest in water.

They carry a useful reputation as well. Many allergy sufferers report tolerating Siberians better than other cats, since the breed tends to produce less of the main cat allergen, though no cat is truly safe for every allergic person.

A Siberian fits an active household. It is playful, fearless, and athletic, a strong jumper that enjoys games, heights, and even water, and it stays sociable and dog-like with family and guests alike. It is slow to mature, filling out over about five years.

The thick triple coat is less work than it looks, needing a thorough brush a couple of times a week and more during the heavy seasonal shed. The breed is generally healthy, though like many large cats it can carry the heart condition HCM, so responsible breeders test their lines.
fblocks: Named for Siberia, the vast cold region of Russia where the breed developed in the wild and in villages.
An ancient forest cat shaped by harsh winters, not by breeders, and named the national cat of Russia.
Active, agile, and people-focused, it enjoys play and even water. The thick coat needs regular brushing, more during seasonal shedding.
A long, water-resistant triple coat with a ruff and bushy tail, in a wide range of colors and patterns.
Slow to mature at up to five years, and often better tolerated by people with allergies, though never truly hypoallergenic.
Give it play, climbing, and company. The Siberian is robust, friendly, and happy in a busy family home.
Brush a few times a week, more in shedding season. Can carry the heart condition HCM, so favor screened breeders.
days: The Siberian is Russia's native cat and wears a triple coat built for snow.
Forests and villages shaped it over centuries. No breeder designed that ruff.
It takes up to five years to fill out. That is a lot of cat still growing.
Belly up on the rug means the room is warm and nobody is a threat.
A thick coat is only a start. The best warmth is a rug beside the stove.
Siberians fetch toys and poke at faucets. Ask who stole the plaid blanket.
Snow at the window, a stove behind, and a big green-eyed cat watching it fall.
last_walk:
The lanterns are lit and the last light goes pink over the pines.
The Siberian sits on the porch rail, ruff full of snow and tail wrapped like a scarf. It has watched the whole winter arrive and minds none of it. Soon it will go in to the stove.
